subject: Micro-trial packaging: seating (concurrent workers) vs. timebox duration — tradeoffs and a short counteroffer
messages:
From: Alyssa Kent <alyssa@novagen.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Novagen Procurement <procurement@novagen.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Micro-trial: can we shift from a 30-day timebox to a seating model?

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the cost breakdown you showed for Redwood Dedicated. We're moving toward a short pilot to validate semantic search and a single-question assistant. A quick question from procurement/ops: would you consider structuring the 30-day micro-trial as a 'concurrent seating' package (N concurrent workers for X hours/day) rather than a pure 30-day timebox?

Pros for us: easier to budget (headcount-like), we can scale workers up/down to simulate load, and it maps better to how we plan to instrument agents. Our ask: a 3-concurrent-seat package for 21 days as a discounted pilot — ideally with one week of engineering office hours rolled in. Is that something you can do, and what are the tradeoffs you see vs. the standard timeboxed approach?

Appreciate a short note — procurement would like the financial comparison to evaluate quickly.

Best,
Alyssa Kent
Head of Platform
Novagen.ai

[Attachment: Novagen_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Kent <alyssa@novagen.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Micro-trial: can we shift from a 30-day timebox to a seating model?

Hi Alyssa — great to hear from you and glad the demo landed. Short answer: yes, we can do a concurrent-seat variant, and we've seen customers prefer it when they care about steady-state concurrency rather than raw token volume. A few practical tradeoffs and what I'd propose: 

- Pricing mechanics: timebox = fixed token/throughput over calendar days. Seating = reserved concurrency (workers) with a capped burst token allowance. Seats map well to latency/throughput guarantees.
- Cost predictability: seats give predictable per-hour cost; timebox gives predictability over calendar days. If your team will be running many short-run experiments per day, seating tends to be cheaper.
- Quality/regression guardrails: with seats we'll pin a model family and provide a snapshot checkpoint; for timeboxes we recommend a token spend cap + KV cache warmup guidance.
- Engineering hours: we can include 8 hours of senior infra/ops support if you sign the pilot within 5 business days.

Counteroffer we can put on the table (novice-friendly, keeps conversion path sensible):
- Option A (Seat-based pilot): 3 concurrent seats, 21 days, includes 1 week (8h) office hours and 200k token burst allowance. Pilot fee: $12,500 (one-off). If you convert to a 6-month paid Dedicated commitment within 30 days of pilot close, we will credit $6,000 against the first invoice.
- Option B (Timebox, for comparison): 30-day timebox with 600k tokens + 4 hours engineering support. Pilot fee: $10,000, conversion credit $4,000.

Both options come with our standard evaluation SLA (99% availability for hosted endpoints used in the pilot) and a 2-week post-pilot diagnostics review. I attached a short proposal and SOW draft for legal/procurement.

If seat-based looks promising, Kimberly can loop in procurement-level pricing and legal to get a quick addendum executed. Does that help? Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk the number assumptions through.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Lead — Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the requirements spreadsheet. A couple of clarifications and a small adjustment on the seat proposal so it maps to our conversion economics: 

- Seat sizing: when you say 3 concurrent seats, do you anticipate continuous 24x7 use or office-hours experiments (09:00–18:00 PT)? We price seats differently for continuous reserved vs business-hours reservation.
- Slight tweak to keep the pilot funnel efficient: we can offer Option A at $11,500 instead of $12,500 if Novagen agrees to a 14-day pilots-onboarding checklist completion and commit to a single conversion evaluation meeting within 10 days post-pilot. Keep the $6k conversion credit if they move to a 6-month Dedicated within 30 days.

If that sounds fair, I'll prepare the addendum and route it through DocuSign. If procurement needs an itemized invoice for internal chargeback, let me know and I’ll attach a line-item export.

Best,
Priyom Das
